children: JPMorgan has identified a potential Bitcoin capitulation signal in the stock market. MicroStrategy
, the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin holder, traded at a record discount to the value of its Bitcoin holdings on Wednesday.
The reading suggests investors are reaching
Historically, such conditions have emerged near market bottoms. However, several sources of selling pressure remain.
What JPMorgan’s Bitcoin Signal Means
MicroStrategy’s valuation fell to 0.88 times its Bitcoin holdings on Wednesday, according to JPMorgan.
The previous record of 0.89 came in late June, when Bitcoin recorded a closing low of $58,525.

image.alt: Bitcoin capitulation signal in Strategy's discount to its Bitcoin holdings. Source: J.P. Morgan Flows & Liquidity

children: The ratio recovered above 1 by early July. MicroStrategy’s own dashboard currently shows a reading of 0.94.However, the company’s removal from MSCI indexes on November 30 will force tracking funds to sell its shares, potentially distorting the signal.
Speculation is also unusually high. Michael Saylor revealed that outstanding MSTR options equaled 61.2% of its market cap, compared with Tesla’s 13.8%.
Are Investors Still Selling Bitcoin?
JPMorgan identified another concerning trend. Investors continued withdrawing money from BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF despite a brief price recovery.
Outflows are now running faster than during the May to June sell-off.
Bitcoin miners are also under financial pressure. JPMorgan estimates that producing one Bitcoin costs approximately $86,000, up from
With Bitcoin trading near $60,470, higher-cost miners may be forced to sell their reserves. Other estimates based on MARA Holdings’ financial disclosures put production costs at $62,862.
Has Bitcoin Reached Its Lowest Price This Cycle?
Galaxy’s research offers a more cautious outlook. Only two of its 13 historical Bitcoin bottom signals had appeared as of November 22.
Across seven previous instances of comparable support breakdowns, Bitcoin’s eventual low came at least 17% lower.
CryptoQuant research head Julio Moreno also warned against expecting an immediate recovery.
“Yes, Bitcoin price is in a value zone, but, historically, a bottoming process and subsequent recovery has taken months, even if there are short-term rallies in the process,” Moreno said.
For investors, Bitcoin’s $58,525 June low remains a critical level. JPMorgan’s signal suggests selling pressure may be approaching exhaustion, but the wider market has yet to confirm a bottom.

title: JPMorgan Spots a Record Bitcoin Signal Through MicroStrategy
